question: Which of one of the following statements about the postnatal growth of the maxilla is correct?
model_reasoning:
The question asks for the correct statement about the postnatal growth of the maxilla. I will evaluate each option based on anatomical and developmental knowledge.
A) Pneumatisation by enlargement of the developing maxillary sinus ceases at puberty. This statement is incorrect. The maxillary sinus continues to grow and pneumatize throughout life, although the most rapid growth occurs during childhood and adolescence.
B) Space is created for the eruption of the permanent molars by resorption of the maxillary tuberosity. This statement is incorrect. Space for the eruption of permanent molars is created by posterior apposition of bone at the maxillary tuberosity, leading to the posterior growth and lengthening of the maxilla, not by resorption.
C) The zygomaticomaxillary sutures contribute to increase in height and length of the maxilla. This statement is correct. The maxilla grows downwards and forwards, and this growth is facilitated by bone deposition at the various circummaxillary sutures, including the zygomaticomaxillary sutures. These sutures allow for the displacement of the maxilla relative to the cranial base, contributing to its overall increase in dimensions (height and length).
D) The intermaxillary suture closes about eight years postnatally. This statement is incorrect. The intermaxillary (midpalatal) suture typically remains open and contributes to transverse maxillary growth well into adolescence and even adulthood, often not fusing completely until much later, if at all, in some individuals.
